name: Data Collection Checklist
description: This module is a pre-completion checklist for data collection work: a short set of checks to run before calling a data collection task done.
content:
This module is a pre-completion checklist for data collection work: a short set of checks to run before calling a data collection task done.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Check that data collection terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
2. Keep data collection outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
3. State assumptions about data collection explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
4. Measure before optimizing any data collection bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
5. When multiple data collection strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
6. Before starting data collection work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
7. Surface known limitations of a chosen data collection approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
8. Document any non-obvious data collection decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
9. Prefer explicit, readable data collection solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
10. Re-check edge cases relevant to data collection (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic data collection advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not silently drop data collection edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not skip documenting data collection assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid introducing new data collection abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated data collection concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for data collection, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
